reference.method: Signed face cones; exact radial polynomials in np.longdouble; 2D Gauss face rule

invariants: tetrahedron subdivision with query at common internal vertex

interpretation: Full 28 is a distinct operator family, not 28 nodal scalar field components
Six physical edge J streams and paired face C streams run through fixed degree 15; no quadrature or global per-pair primitive/moment scratch
26 named double accumulators cover two scalar potentials, two vectors and three symmetric tensors; three Cov entries are duplicated only on output
All final subsets and full kernels have zero runtime local allocation and measured local LD/ST sectors
The full family has 188 registers (192 allocated), versus 128 Hessian-only, 136 gradient-only and 144 values-only
Smaller blocks reduce 8192-pair latency approximately twofold but do not raise large-batch achieved occupancy or materially improve throughput
Mixed geometry executes fewer predicated arithmetic operations per pair but runs slower, consistent with divergent edge/support paths
No production dispatch, 2D backend, raw-fp32 policy or solver integration was changed
limitations: Experimental device functions and studies; native 3D compact boundary-limit failures still require a guarded production fix
W6 volume tetrahedra and this 28-output contract only; no generic higher-degree, arbitrary kernel, surface-triangle or quadrature-fp32 performance claim
Independent references use empirical successive-order convergence, not a universal error bound or double-machine-epsilon certification
Counts are executed add/mul/FMA arithmetic (FMA=2); division, root, transcendental, integer and control costs are not converted to FLOPs
Mixed sample uses 256 static tetrahedra, random queries/supports and indices; it is not a localized accepted-pair distribution or complete solver step
Static geometry preparation is host fp64; warm timings exclude preparation/JIT/search/assembly; transfer timer includes host input validation/allocation/upload/kernel/readback
At 1048576 pairs, full output is 224 MiB and inputs plus output 260 MiB; explicit readback remains much slower than device-only evaluation
Serialized measurements with unlocked clocks/caches and desktop activity; sub-percent launch timing changes do not establish a preferred large-batch size
next_step: Extract the validated regular-flux/edge-line stream into a production W6 fp64 device path with explicit request/order mapping; reproduce the native compact rotated-boundary failures as regressions, validate the supported dispatch on CPU/CUDA and leave generic kernels on existing paths until separately checked
